transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lisa Chen (CTO - Nimbus), Marcus Graham (Head of ML), Evelyn Park (VP Product)
Recording: internal/fireflies/ff-2025-08-21-nimbus-001.mp3 (auto)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on cost modeling and unit economics. Customer wants to understand per-token pricing, batching/caching knobs, expected latency tradeoffs, and a short benchmark plan to validate cost/latency on their workload. Agreement to exchange traces and run a 2-hour benchmark on a Dedicated pool or Nimbus VPC. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics:
- Workload characterization: token distribution, seq lengths, QPS
- Cost model: per-token estimates, GPU types, quantization impact
- Batching/KV cache: impact on unit economics and latency SLOs
- Benchmark plan: inputs, metrics, timeline
- Security/compliance and deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, I think we've got about an hour for this. Introductions quick - I'm Alex, AE on the account, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Priya Desai: Hi all, thanks. I can jump into the cost modeling side and the benchmark plan, walk through what we typically measure.
[00:00:20] Lisa Chen: Great. I'm Lisa, CTO. Marcus and Evelyn are on from product and ML. We're here because we need to scope a short POC to validate unit economics before we commit to Dedicated.
[00:00:30] Marcus Graham: Yep, specifically we want to know per-token cost for our reranking flows and a typical chat flow. Also latency constraints - 95th under 300ms if possible.
[00:00:40] Evelyn Park: And timeline — we want to decide by mid-September, so a 2-3 week POC would be ideal.

[00:01:00] Priya Desai: Cool. Quick question on current infra: what are you running today for inference? Host? self-host?
[00:01:08] Marcus Graham: Right now mostly a mix — prototypes on EC2 with CPU endpoints, a couple internal tests on SageMaker with small GPU nodes. No production LLM infra.
[00:01:18] Lisa Chen: We want to avoid building the whole runtime. That's why we're looking at Redwood Dedicated or Private. Data residency might push us to VPC but we'll see.

[00:01:30] Alex Martin: Understood. For cost modeling the key inputs are token profile (avg tokens per request, max seq), QPS, concurrency, and whether caching/prefix KV helps. Can you give us a ballpark token distribution?
[00:01:45] Marcus Graham: Ballpark: batching/rerank requests average 120 tokens in, 400 tokens out; chat messages average 30 tokens in, 60 tokens out. QPS varies — peak ~8 TPS for rerank, chat is spiky around 25 TPS but lower concurrent.
[00:02:05] Priya Desai: That's helpful. We'll need sample traces but we can start with those numbers. For per-token cost modeling we assume two options: hosted (per-token) and Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity). For Dedicated we model on a per-GPU hour basis and convert to per-token via throughput estimates.

[00:02:25] [00:02:40] Alex Martin: Important note — quantization and optimized kernels change throughput a lot. On A100 with float16 we see X tokens/sec; H100 and int8 can be 1.8-2x faster for certain models. So in the cost sheet we'll include a conservative and optimistic throughput estimate.
[00:02:58] Marcus Graham: When you say X tokens/sec, can you give ranges? We need to plug numbers into our finance model.
[00:03:05] Priya Desai: Sure, rough numbers - for a 7B open model on a single A100 (fp16) with batching we typically get ~3k-6k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and KV usage. With H100 or optimized int8 it's maybe 5k-10k tokens/sec. For 13B models it's lower, 1.5k-3.5k tokens/sec on A100. These are rough; we'll run benchmarks to narrow.

[00:03:32] Evelyn Park: How does batching affect latency? I mean we can't have large batch sizes if we need low 95th latency.
[00:03:40] Priya Desai: Right — batching increases throughput but adds queuing latency. Redwood supports continuous batching and you can set latency SLOs; the runtime will dynamically batch under those constraints. Also prefix/KV caching is major: for chat flows with repeated prefixes, cache hits reduce compute dramatically, improving per-token economics while keeping latency low.
[00:04:00] Lisa Chen: So for our reranker where inputs are short but outputs long, what knobs should we tune?
[00:04:07] Priya Desai: For rerank we recommend smaller batches but higher concurrency, because outputs are bigger. Also consider offloading some pre-filtering to a lightweight model to reduce candidate set. Quantization (4-bit/8-bit) can lower cost but verify quality on your evals.

[00:04:25] [00:04:40] Marcus Graham: Let's talk numbers: if we assume 8 TPS rerank with 400 tokens out and 120 in, what does that translate to in per-token cost?
[00:04:48] Alex Martin: We'll do per-token via two paths: Hosted per-token pricing (straight multiply) vs Dedicated where cost = (reserved GPU cost + infra overhead) / total tokens served over commit. For example, a conservative Dedicated calc: A100 reserved cost $X/hour (we'll put actual in the sheet), amortize over expected utilization (say 60-80%). Then tokens/hour = tokens/sec * 3600. So per-token = cost/hour ÷ tokens/hour.
[00:05:15] Priya Desai: To make that concrete, if you get 4k tokens/sec average -> 14.4M tokens/hour. If an A100 reserved is $5/hour (placeholder) and infra overhead total $6/hour, total $11/hr => $11 / 14.4M ≈ $0.00000076 per token, then multiply for prompt+completion tokens. Hosted might be e.g. $0.00003 per token depending on plan, so there's a crossover based on utilization. We'll provide a sensitivity table.

[00:05:50] Marcus Graham: That per-token on Dedicated seems tiny but it's sensitive to utilization and sequence length. We need to see 95th latency too; if we crank batching to reach that throughput do we violate 300ms?
[00:06:00] Priya Desai: We will include latency-aware scenarios. For low-latency SLOs (95th < 300ms) you'll typically run with smaller batch windows and potentially more GPUs. That raises cost per token; we'll show cost vs latency curve.

[00:06:20] Evelyn Park: For security, we will likely require VPC Private deployment for production. How does that affect POC?
[00:06:28] Alex Martin: For POC we can do either: hosted with private networking to pull sample traces (if allowed) or spin up Redwood Private in your VPC for a short benchmark run. Private requires a bit more setup (network + KMS), but we can facilitate a short trial deployment. We'll include setup time in the timeline.

[00:06:45] Lisa Chen: What's the typical timeline you recommend? We said mid-September decision.
[00:06:50] Priya Desai: Suggestion: 1) this week - exchange traces and confirm metrics; 2) next week - we run baseline hosted benchmarks with your sample traces (1-2 days); 3) week after - run Dedicated/VPC benchmark (2-3 days, includes setup); 4) final week - review results, cost model and decision. So total ~2.5-3 weeks.

[00:07:18] [00:07:32] Alex Martin: For the benchmark plan we'll collect: sample requests (JSON), tokenization distribution, QPS patterns (hourly), success criteria (cost per 1M tokens, 95th latency < 300ms, throughput target). Please add any other success metrics.
[00:07:48] Marcus Graham: Also include stability (error rate under peak). And memory/KV cache hit rate expectations for chat.

[00:07:58] Priya Desai: Noted. The benchmark artifacts we'll share: a runner (docker), a Jupyter with the analysis, and a template CSV for traces. We'll also share an example cost model where you can change variables: GPU type, utilization, batch size, quantization, and it will recompute per-token.

[00:08:20] Lisa Chen: Any gotchas with quantization for our models? We use a proprietary reranker that was trained with fp16.
[00:08:27] Priya Desai: Quality regressions are the main risk. We'll recommend running your eval suite against quantized checkpoints; sometimes 4-bit works fine, sometimes you need mixed-precision. We'll capture quality delta and fold that into the cost/benefit analysis.

[00:08:45] [00:09:00] Marcus Graham: What about caching? If we have high prefix reuse for chat, how big is the win?
[00:09:06] Priya Desai: If you get 60-70% KV cache hit rates on chat, compute can drop drastically — compute for cached tokens is near zero aside from KV fetch cost. That can improve per-token by 2-5x depending on hit rate. We'll run a simulation based on your traces.

[00:09:30] Evelyn Park: For the POC, what would success look like?
[00:09:35] Alex Martin: Twofold: 1) technical: we demonstrate we can meet the latency/throughput targets on a representative workload with acceptable error rates, and 2) economic: we show a cost model that meets your budget thresholds or clearly shows what you'd pay for Dedicated vs Hosted. If both are true you can move to a pilot commit.

[00:09:58] [00:10:12] Marcus Graham: Budget — our finance said we want a target of $X per active user per month but for now translate that into a per-token cap: for the rerank flow we want < $0.02 per inference (all tokens included).
[00:10:25] Priya Desai: We'll map that to per-token targets given your token counts. We'll include a sensitivity where if per-infer cost is above target we show options: higher quantization, more caching, or move to bigger instance counts to reduce latency at higher cost.

[00:10:42] Alex Martin: I'll call out a few concrete deliverables — cost model spreadsheet with scenarios, benchmark scripts + results, and a recommendation doc summarizing tradeoffs and deployment mode.

[00:10:55] Lisa Chen: Sounds good. Any questions from Redwood side about dataset sharing or access?
[00:11:02] Priya Desai: We usually ask for anonymized traces. If anything sensitive, put them in your VPC and we can instruct on how to run the benchmark there. For POC we don't need production data.

[00:11:15] Marcus Graham: We'll anonymize and strip PII. Expect a 1-week trace extract.

[00:11:22] [00:11:35] Alex Martin: Cool. One other note — we'll provide a Hosted price comparison. Hosted is easier to start with but at scale Dedicated or Private usually has better unit economics depending on utilization. We'll model the crossover point in the sheet.

[00:11:50] Evelyn Park: Competitors asked about: we looked at Anthropic for quality, OpenAI for latency, and SageMaker for an integrated infra option. Please include any known performance differences in your notes.

[00:12:05] Priya Desai: We'll keep that high level; we don't have exact apples-to-apples numbers for closed models but we can summarize expected tradeoffs.

[00:12:15] Alex Martin: Ok let's recap and owners: Alex will send the cost model and dedicated pricing, Priya will send the benchmark runner and template, Marcus will provide traces, Lisa will confirm security distribution list. We'll aim for the first benchmark runs next week.

[00:12:32] Lisa Chen: Thanks. That works.

[00:12:36] Marcus Graham: Thanks all.

[00:12:40] Priya Desai: Thanks, bye.

[00:12:45] Alex Martin: Bye everyone.

Post-call notes (auto): Transcript has typical ASR artifacts; specific numeric placeholders (gpu $/hour) are estimates and will be replaced with actual pricing in the shared sheet. The POC will focus on two workloads: rerank and chat, with success metrics: cost per inference < $0.02 for rerank (customer target), 95th latency < 300ms for chat, and stability (error rate < 1%).
